confirmed: Primary indexed archive pages expose explicit 25 October broadcast dates and clock ranges, but fresh raw television-home and dated-archive requests both return HTTP 403.
The programme page distinguishes linear television transmission from WebTV1/2/3; those signals cannot be combined.
The official open-data documentation advertises laws/taxonomies, not a television-guide method.
The Parliament-designated GRNET embed is reachable and declares public event and date-filtered schedule metadata routes.
GRNET event 6022 describes continuous parliamentary web television, not one programme: the event spans 2024–2028 and all six room sessions span multiple years.
The inspected schedule component passes YYYY-MM-DD calendar-date strings to its public range endpoints.
The 25–31 October ordinary schedule returns 3 entries and the epresence schedule 15; neither contains event 6022 or a Parliament-named programme.

confirmed: The previously retrieved 26–27 October grid contains 13 future programmes with duration zero.
All nested future transmission/media durations in that payload are also zero.
Nested media start/end clocks are equal midnight placeholders and can differ from programme broadcast dates.
Fresh public application-script inspection did not establish another authoritative future programme-end contract.
An asset or clipping date is not a channel broadcast time; future transmission placeholders must not override the programme start.
sources.decision: Retain the existing positive source-duration policy and exact EBS channel scope. No safe future end alternative was established; no next-start inference, nested asset-date substitution or fixed-length padding.
